text: I woke at 3:17. The bakery is all yeast smell and quiet. Marisol put the loaves in the oven and saw the book again, The Borrowers in the wicker basket by the back door. Every Thursday for six weeks somebody has put it back here and not the library two blocks over. No name, no card, just the book, faintly smells like rain and woodsmoke. This time a folded note slipped between pages 84 and 85. She put her floury hands on the counter for a second then opened it: i cant make it to the library before closing. Please keep it another week. I like knowing its warm. Looked at the basket and the cinnamon rolls out on the rack still hot. She picked the one with the most icing, wrapped it in wax paper, put the note back in the book and left them both by the door. Then she flipped the sign to OPEN and got to the coffee.
